notes.title: Greeks for Options – Part A (Delta)
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks
notes.description: What the Greeks measure, and delta in full — its sign and range for all four positions, its reading as the probability of finishing in the money, and how time to maturity and volatility move it.

notes.title: Greeks for Options – Part B (Gamma)
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks
notes.description: Gamma as the sensitivity of delta — why it peaks at the money, why it is always positive, why it favours the long and punishes the short, and why its relationship with time is the opposite of delta's.

notes.title: Greeks for Options – Part C (Theta)
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks
notes.description: Theta and time decay — why it is negative for the long and positive for the short, the intrinsic/extrinsic split that explains it, and why decay is fastest at the money and accelerates into expiry.

notes.title: Greeks for Options – Part D (Vega)
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks
notes.description: Vega and implied volatility — why volatility is a friend to every long option and an enemy to every short, why vega peaks at the money, and why long-dated options carry more of it.

notes.title: Greeks for Options – Part E (Rho)
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks
notes.description: Rho and the risk-free rate — why calls gain and puts lose when rates rise, why rho is highest in the money rather than at the money, and when it matters at all. Closes with all five Greeks side by side.
headings: All five Greeks, side by side

notes.title: Delta Hedging

notes.title: Gamma Hedging
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks

notes.title: Delta-Gamma Hedging

notes.title: Vega Hedging
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks

notes.title: Theta Hedging
notes.path: Finance / Quant Finance Bootcamp / Risk Management Greeks

notes.title: Rho Hedging

notes.title: Measures of Central Tendency
notes.description: A measure of central tendency answers the first question you ask of any dataset: where is it centered? There are three answers, and the gaps between them are as informative as the numbers themselves.
headings: The key difference: robustness to outliers

notes.title: Measures of Dispersion
notes.description: Center isn't enough. Two datasets can share the exact same mean and be completely different — one tightly clustered, one wildly spread. Dispersion measures that spread, and for a quant it's where risk lives.

notes.title: Standard Deviation
